transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because even after I do my safety check, I keep thinking I missed something on the cab. Like somebody could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied. I know I checked, but the thought just keeps coming back, especially when I’m driving or trying to study, and I can’t get it to stop.
When this thought about missing something on the cab pops up, do you find yourself going back to re-check the truck, or doing some other repeated action, to try to make the worry go away?

Yeah. Before I can take a ride, I go around the car checking the tires, lights, doors, the meter, and my paperwork over and over. Sometimes I take pictures too. If it doesn’t feel right, I start the whole check again, even if passengers are waiting and I’m already late.
About how much time each day would you say you spend on these checking behaviors and repeated re-checking?

A lot—probably a couple of hours most days, sometimes more. I keep circling the car checking the tires, lights, doors, meter, and paperwork, and I’ll take pictures. If it still doesn’t feel right, I start all over, even with people waiting and me running late.
Do you feel that this checking and re-checking is more than what's really needed, or does it feel like a genuinely reasonable amount of caution to you?

I mean, I know it’s probably more than most people would do. But if I don’t go around and check the tires, lights, doors, meter, and paperwork again—and sometimes take pictures—it doesn’t feel right. I end up restarting even when passengers are waiting and I’m already late.
How long have you been experiencing these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors—days, weeks, or months?
I'm not really sure how long it's been. I know it's been happening, but I haven't kept track of when it started.
Would you say these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors have been happening on most days for at least the past two weeks?

Yeah, it’s been most days. Even after I do the safety check, I keep thinking I missed something on the cab—that somebody could get hurt or my boss will think I lied. It just keeps going in my head when I’m driving or trying to study.
Would you say these thoughts and checking rituals have caused you significant distress or gotten in the way of your work, driving schedule, or personal life?

Yeah. I’ve lost rides and gotten warnings because I can’t get on the road on time. The checking eats up so much of the day that my CDL studying keeps getting pushed back too. And I barely see my friends anymore—I’m either behind on work or trying to catch up after all the delays.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits classic OCD presentation with mixed obsessions and compulsions: intrusive, recurrent thoughts about having missed a safety issue on his cab (obsession) causing significant anxiety, followed by repetitive checking behaviors (compulsions - checking tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork, photographing) performed to neutralize the distress.
